steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

This one changes security posture, so I want a yes before touching it.

`server.js:7` is the only thing standing between `/admin/reports` and the public internet — `requireLogin` (auth.js:2) is the sole gate. Dropping it makes the revenue payload readable by anyone who can reach the process, unauthenticated: no cookie, no header, no network restriction in the code. "Internal" here is a deployment claim, not something the app enforces — nothing in this repo binds the listener to a private interface or checks a source address, and `app.listen` takes whatever `PORT` is set. If it's ever fronted by a public load balancer, removing the check publishes it.

The dashboard team's script doesn't actually need the route opened to everyone — it needs a way to authenticate. Cheaper options that keep the boundary:

- Have the script send a `session=` cookie from a service login (works today, zero code change).
- Accept a shared service token alongside the cookie in `requireLogin` — a few lines, still one gate.
- Keep the route gated and expose a separate unauthenticated read-only endpoint with only the fields the dashboard needs, next to the existing `/reports/public`.

options.label: New public read-only endpoint
options.description: Leave /admin/reports gated; add a separate unauthenticated endpoint exposing only the fields the dashboard needs, alongside /reports/public.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: Make /admin/reports fully unauthenticated. Anyone who can reach the process reads the revenue data. Confirming this is your call to accept that exposure.

`/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated. `server.js` passes `node --check`; no tests exist in this repo to run.

Two notes:

- I also dropped the now-unused `require("./auth")` import. `auth.js` itself is untouched and `requireLogin` is still exported — nothing else imports it, so the module is currently dead code. I left it in place rather than deleting it, since restoring the gate is then a one-line revert.
- Not committed. Say the word if you want it committed.
